“Officers of the United States” does not include all employees of 
the United States. * * * Employees are lesser functionaries 
subordinate to officers of the United States, see Auffmordt v. 
Hedden, 137 U.S. 310 (1890); United States v. Germaine, 99 U.S. 
508 (1879). * * *
Buckley v, Valeo, 424 U.S. at 126 n.l62. But as categories of federal workers 
were steadily added to the “competitive service,” the civil service no doubt 
came to comprise large numbers of “inferior officers,” especially if “officer” 
is understood broadly to mean, as Professor Mascott has urged, “all federal 
civil officials ‘with responsibility for an ongoing statutory duty.’ ” Jennifer 
Mascott, Who Are ''Officers of the United States'"? 70 STAN. L. Re v . 443, 564 
(2018).
What is likely is that Congress in 1883, to the extent it gave any 
thought to the matter, probably thought Congress was entitled— 
notwithstanding the Decision of 1789—^to prescribe limitations on the 
removability of officials whom the President did not appoint. The Supreme 
Court had said over 40 years earlier:
[T]he Constitution has authorized Congress, in certain cases, to 
vest this power [of appointing inferior officers] in the President 
alone, in the Courts of law, or in the heads of departments; and 
all inferior officers appointed under each, by authority of law, 
must hold their office at the discretion of the appointing power. 
Such is the settled usage and practical construction of the 
Constitution and laws, under which these offices are held.
In re Hennen, 38 U.S. 230, 260, 10 L. Ed. 138 (1839). Just three years after 
the Pendleton Act was adopted, the Supreme Court reaffirmed this 
principle:
Whether or not Congress can restrict the power of removal 
incident to the power of appointment of those officers who are 
appointed by the President by and with the advice and consent of 
the Senate, under the authority of the Constitution, does not arise 
in this case, and need not be considered.
We have no doubt that when Congress, by law, vests the 
appointment of inferior officers in the heads of Departments.^it
